name: Lepakshi Haritha Hotel Restaurant (AP Tourism)
why_it_matters: The restaurant at APTDC's Haritha Hotel — the only proper hotel in Lepakshi, about 450m from the 16th-century Veerabhadra Temple. It serves simple Andhra meals and is the single most reliable sit-down meal in the village; standalone restaurants in Lepakshi are very limited, so the tourism hotel restaurant is the dependable bet.
insider_tip: Lepakshi is a tiny temple village — most visitors do it as a day trip from Bengaluru or Hindupur. If you want lunch here rather than carrying food, the Haritha restaurant is the safe choice; pre-order on busy weekends.

name: Lepakshi Restaurant
why_it_matters: A simple village restaurant near the Veerabhadra Temple entrance serving both vegetarian and non-vegetarian food — rice, roti, curry, biryani and sweets. In a village with barely a handful of eateries, it is the practical walk-in meal stop for temple visitors, open 7am-9pm.
insider_tip: Roughly ₹100 a head for a basic meal. Hours are tied to temple footfall — eat at standard meal times rather than expecting all-day service. Cash; carry small notes as in any small village.

name: Sri Venkateswara Canteen (temple complex)
signature_dish: Simple veg meal (rice, sambar, rasam, curd)
why_it_matters: A small canteen within the Veerabhadra Temple premises serving a simple pure-veg lunch and dinner — rice, sambar, rasam, curd and pickle. For pilgrims doing the temple at midday, it is the on-site option that saves a walk out of the complex; basic temple-canteen fare, not destination dining.
insider_tip: Open only at meal windows — roughly 12-2pm and 7-9pm — so time the temple visit around it. Strictly vegetarian. If you arrive between services, the village's Lepakshi Restaurant is the fallback.
